term: categorical reason versus contingent instrumental reason
definition: A categorical-reason requirement would supply each relevant rational agent with a normative reason independent of contingent ends. InstrumentalReason x a in these tests is instead an independently supplied instrumental reason for that agent; a distinct pro-tanto normative-reason relation is not encoded by this signature. The primitive defines neither actual desire, motivation, obligation, decisive priority nor impartial rightness. The consistency models witness only that the selected realist fragments coexist with absence of an instrumental reason for one agent, not that categorical reasons fail or that the authors reject every non-instrumental reason.
